sources.entry: stronghold - Easily configure MacOS security settings from the terminal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/alichtman/stronghold) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
stronghold - Easily configure macOS security settings from the terminal.

summary.one_liner: stronghold is a terminal tool that walks you through hardening macOS security settings such as the firewall, Gatekeeper, metadata storage, and user safety options.
summary.what_it_does: It is a Python script (stronghold.py) that prompts you through a series of macOS security configuration choices, each with a short explanation. The options cover the firewall (turning it on, enabling logging, enabling stealth mode), general system protection (Gatekeeper, blocking automatic software whitelisting, disabling the Captive Portal Assistant), and user metadata (clearing and disabling language modeling data, QuickLook and Downloads metadata, and the SiriAnalytics database). It also covers user safety settings such as locking the Mac when the screen saver starts, showing all file extensions and hidden files in Finder, disabling cloud saving by default, and disabling printer sharing. A -lockdown flag applies the secure configuration without user interaction. It can be installed with pip or run from a binary on the Releases tab.
use_cases: Hardening a new Mac with recommended security settings
Turning on the macOS firewall and stealth mode from the terminal
Clearing language modeling and QuickLook metadata on a Mac
Showing file extensions and hidden files in Finder
Scripting a non-interactive macOS security lockdown
how_to_run: Or download the stronghold binary from the Releases tab
notable: Interactive, explains each setting with a short rationale before you choose
Non-interactive -lockdown mode for applying the full configuration at once
Covers firewall, Gatekeeper, metadata cleanup, and Finder visibility settings in one tool
Also distributed as a standalone binary on the Releases tab
caveats: Designed for macOS Sierra and High Sierra; the README says it has not yet been tested on macOS Mojave
Only macOS is covered; the README makes no claims about other platforms
